questions.question: During electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride, predict the products at both electrodes and justify them.
questions.modelAnswer:
Hydrogen forms at the cathode because sodium is more reactive than hydrogen, so water/H⁺ is reduced.
Chlorine forms at the anode because chloride ions are present and are oxidised: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻.

questions.question:
Describe electrorefining of copper using impure copper and pure copper electrodes in copper sulfate solution.
Include electrode changes and half equations.
questions.modelAnswer:
Impure copper is positive anode.
Pure copper is negative cathode.
At anode Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻, so it loses mass and impurities form sludge/remain.
At cathode Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu, so pure copper deposits and cathode gains mass.
Cu²⁺ concentration remains approximately constant.

questions.question: Explain why cryolite reduces the energy cost of aluminium extraction.
questions.modelAnswer:
Cryolite lowers the melting point of aluminium oxide, so less electrical energy is needed to keep the electrolyte molten.
This reduces cost.
